solution_full: For any $x$: $\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}=\dfrac{f(h)}{h}+x^{2}+xh\to-3+x^{2}$ as $h\to0$. So $f'(x)=x^{2}-3$ and, with $f(0)=0$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}-3x$.

Critical points: $x=0$ and $x=\pm\dfrac{3}{\sqrt5}$. Sign of $G'$: negative on $\left(-\infty,-\frac{3}{\sqrt5}\right)$, positive on $\left(-\frac{3}{\sqrt5},0\right)$, negative on $\left(0,\frac{3}{\sqrt5}\right)$, positive after. So $x=\pm\frac{3}{\sqrt5}$ are local minima and $x=0$ a local maximum.

Explicitly $G(x)=\left[\dfrac{t^{4}}{12}-\dfrac{3t^{2}}{2}\right]_{x}^{2x}=\dfrac{15x^{4}}{12}-\dfrac{9x^{2}}{2}=\dfrac54x^{4}-\dfrac92x^{2}$, which tends to $+\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$, so the least of the local minima is the minimum value.
originality_note: New: a cubic functional equation fixed by a limit, followed by the extremum of the integral of f over the moving interval [x, 2x] (way 5). Closest known: f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y) + 2xy type equations; minima of int_0^x f. Different because: the window [x, 2x] scales with x, giving G' = 2f(2x) - f(x) and a quartic G.
